overview: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple, popularly known as Bhadrachalam Temple, is one of the most revered pilgrimage destinations dedicated to Lord Sri Rama in India. Located on the serene banks of the sacred Godavari River in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, it is regarded as the spiritual heart of Rama devotion in South India and is affectionately called Dakshina Ayodhya ('Ayodhya of the South'). The deity appears in the rare Vaikuntha Rama form with four divine arms. The temple is deeply connected with the legendary devotee Bhakta Ramadasu (Kancharla Gopanna) and attracts millions of devotees every year.
summary: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple, popularly known as Bhadrachalam Temple, is one of India's most revered temples dedicated to Lord Sri Rama. Located on the banks of the Godavari River in Bhadradri Kothagudem district of Telangana, the temple is celebrated for its association with the Ramayana, Bhakta Bhadra, and Bhakta Ramadasu. It attracts millions of devotees every year, particularly during Sri Rama Navami, when the celestial wedding of Lord Rama and Sita (Sri Sita Rama Kalyanam) is performed. Known for its unique Vaikuntha Rama idol, rich historical significance, grand festivals, sacred rituals, and well-organized pilgrim facilities, it is one of the most visited pilgrimage destinations in South India.

history.content: According to ancient legends, the temple's origins date back to the Treta Yuga. Bhakta Bhadra, the son of Mount Meru, performed intense penance on the hill now known as Bhadrachalam, praying for the divine vision of Lord Rama. Since Lord Rama was engaged in fulfilling His earthly duties during His incarnation, He promised Bhadra that He would grant him darshan after completing His mission. After the victory over Ravana and the return from Lanka, Lord Rama appeared before Bhakta Bhadra accompanied by Goddess Sita and Lord Lakshmana, blessing the sage with eternal salvation. The hill became known as Bhadragiri and the settlement Bhadrachalam ('the hill of Bhadra').
legends: Bhakta Bhadra, son of Mount Meru, performed intense penance on the hill seeking the divine vision of Lord Rama.

The hill became known as Bhadragiri and the settlement as Bhadrachalam.

history.content: The present temple owes much of its glory to Kancharla Gopanna, popularly known as Bhakta Ramadasu, a devoted follower of Lord Rama who served as the Tahsildar of Palvancha during the reign of the Qutb Shahi dynasty in the seventeenth century. Deeply moved by the neglected condition of the ancient shrine, Ramadasu utilized government tax revenue to reconstruct the temple. When Sultan Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) learned of the expenditure, Ramadasu was imprisoned in Golconda Fort for nearly twelve years, during which he composed numerous devotional songs praising Lord Rama. According to tradition, Lord Rama and Lakshmana appeared in royal attire before the Sultan's court and repaid the exact amount using gold coins bearing the divine seal; astonished, Tana Shah released Ramadasu and became a devotee of Lord Rama.
legends: Ramadasu used government tax revenue to reconstruct the temple and was imprisoned in Golconda Fort for nearly twelve years.

sthala_puranam: Bhakta Bhadra, son of Mount Meru, performed intense penance on this hill for the divine vision of Lord Rama. The Lord promised to grant darshan after completing His earthly mission. Following His victory over Ravana, Lord Rama appeared before Bhadra accompanied by Goddess Sita and Lord Lakshmana and manifested upon the hill, granting the sage eternal salvation. The hill thus became Bhadragiri, and the place came to be called Bhadrachalam, 'the hill of Bhadra'.
religious_significance: Bhadrachalam is one of the holiest temples dedicated to Lord Sri Rama, lovingly called Dakshina Ayodhya. Unlike temples associated with the removal of a particular dosha, it is revered as a place where devotees seek Lord Rama's blessings for righteousness (Dharma), family harmony, courage, prosperity, and inner peace. It symbolizes the triumph of truth over evil and the ideals of Dharma upheld by Lord Rama. Its association with Bhakta Bhadra and Bhakta Ramadasu makes it a powerful symbol of unwavering devotion and divine grace.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe sincere prayers at Bhadrachalam help remove obstacles from life, strengthen family relationships, and bring harmony to households. Couples pray for a happy married life, students seek wisdom and success, farmers pray for abundant harvests, and businesspersons seek prosperity. It is considered auspicious for those facing emotional distress, financial difficulties, or major life decisions. The sacred Godavari River beside the temple enhances its significance — a holy bath before entering the temple is regarded as purifying.

architecture: A magnificent example of traditional South Indian Dravidian architecture, the temple is situated on the sacred Bhadragiri Hill along the banks of the Godavari River. The towering Rajagopuram is adorned with intricate carvings of gods, goddesses, and scenes from the Ramayana. The sanctum houses Lord Sri Rama in the rare Vaikuntha Rama form, accompanied by Goddess Sita and Lord Lakshmana. The complex contains separate shrines for Lord Hanuman, Garuda, Andal, Alwars, and other deities, with spacious mandapams used for daily rituals, special sevas, and the grand celestial wedding. Wide corridors, a large pradakshina path, and decorated halls provide a peaceful atmosphere for worship.

darshan_and_tickets.general_darshan: General (Sarva) Darshan is free of cost for all devotees.
darshan_and_tickets.special_darshan: Special Darshan tickets available at ₹50, ₹100, and ₹250 (VIP Ticket).
darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Tickets for sevas and darshan can be purchased at the temple ticket counters or booked online through the official temple website. During Sri Rama Navami and other major festivals, special arrangements are made to manage the large influx of pilgrims.

dress_code: Devotees are expected to wear traditional and modest attire. Men are encouraged to wear dhoti, kurta, or traditional Indian clothing; women are advised to wear sarees, salwar kameez, or other modest traditional dresses. Tight-fitting or revealing clothes, including shorts, sleeveless tops, skirts, jeans, and T-shirts, are discouraged, especially for the inner temple or special sevas. Footwear must be removed before entering, silence should be maintained, and photography may be restricted inside the sanctum.
facilities: Senior citizen assistance and separate festival queues

accommodation.availability: Temple-operated guest houses and cottages offer clean and affordable lodging, convenient for early morning darshan, Nitya Kalyanam, or Sri Rama Navami celebrations. Numerous private budget, family, deluxe, and premium hotels are also available in Bhadrachalam town.
accommodation.booking_process: Rooms can be booked through the temple's official website or at the accommodation counter. Advance online booking is strongly recommended during weekends and festivals (Sri Rama Navami, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Brahmotsavam) as rooms fill quickly.
accommodation.first_come_basis: Limited walk-in accommodation may be available at temple counters on a first-come basis, but advance online booking is strongly recommended especially during festivals and weekends.
accommodation.price_range: Temple-managed rooms generally ₹300–₹1,000 per night (AC and larger family rooms higher). Private hotels and lodges ₹800–₹3,000+ per night.
nearby_options: Private budget, family, and premium hotels in Bhadrachalam town

best_time_to_visit: October to March (October–February is excellent), with pleasant cool weather. Best days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. Best time: 5:30 AM–8:00 AM; evening option 3:30 PM–5:00 PM. Sri Rama Navami, Vaikunta Ekadasi, Brahmotsavam, and Hanuman Jayanti are especially auspicious but very crowded.

travel.road: Approximately 320 km from Hyderabad, reachable by road with frequent TGSRTC buses from Hyderabad, Warangal, Khammam, Karimnagar, and Nizamabad, and APSRTC buses from Vijayawada, Rajahmundry, Visakhapatnam, and Eluru. The scenic drive passes through forests, rivers, and rural landscapes.

travel.air: Nearest airports are Rajahmundry Airport (~185 km) and Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~310–320 km). Taxis and bus services are available from both airports.

top_reviews: Tripadvisor (PuvvadaS, 5/5, 'The famous temple of lord rams named as the district also'): 'This is very ancient temple renovated and constructed by saint bhaktha ramadas during nizams period. He was jailed for money spent and historical proofs exists for release of ramadas by lord rama and laxman by themselves paying golden rama coins. 2 coins still available in temple. Other points to see are lord laxminarasimha temple, saibaba temple, Parnasala, Manuguru neelakanteswara temple, mallur laxminarasimha swamy temple, palvoncha balaji temples, peddamma temple, are nearby temples. Picnic spots include pamuleru river beach, kondayagudem temple and ghat, mothe temple and island, kinnerasani dam and coatings. Water falls are at manuguru and bogata during rainy season. Bogata water fall is excellent and near cherla. For visiting all these places personal vehicle recommended.'

Tripadvisor (ananthshenoy, 5/5): 'A really must visit temple for all. Pls visit only during winters during Nov to feb as other seasons are sultry. The temple is beautiful and the deity specially is of Sri Rama with sita, Lakshmana and his brothers is must see. The temple is peaceful and the deity is very well decorated. There is also a museum of the jewellery of the deity given by various people during the years and is a must see. Pls do not miss this. This is only seen in this temple and I have not seen this in any other temple. One can also buy prasadam laddu if one wants. On the whole a very nice temple to visit.'

Tripadvisor (UdhayakumarG, 5/5, 'Only reason to visit Bhadrachalam'): 'The temple is the only reason to visit Bhadrachalam. Morning is crowded, evening is totally free even on saturday evening. Did not even stand in queue for evening Free Dharsan. Laddu prasad is wonderful.'

Tripadvisor (AnoopBoddeti, 5/5, 'Badhrachalam'): 'Temple is good with basic facilities to the pilgrimages. Never book devasthanam rooms as they are not well maintained instead book hotels which are nearby to the temple.'

Tripadvisor (Positive summary): 'Visited Bhadrachalam a nice quiet and calm but a powerful temple with spouse. Performed rituals and poojas in the temple. All types of devas attended and felt happy. The temple is situated on the banks of the Godavari River, and the location itself is a divine experience. Sri Rama Navami celebrations are spectacular with the celestial wedding of Lord Rama and Sita — a must-see for any devotee.'

faq.question: Where is Bhadrachalam Temple located?
faq.answer: Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple is located in Bhadrachalam, Bhadradri Kothagudem district, Telangana, on the banks of the Godavari River.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped at Bhadrachalam Temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Lord Sri Rama, worshipped along with Goddess Sita and Lord Lakshmana in the rare Vaikuntha Rama form.

faq.question: Why is Bhadrachalam called Dakshina Ayodhya?
faq.answer: The temple is closely associated with the Ramayana and is believed to be one of the most sacred places connected to Lord Rama in South India, earning it the title Dakshina Ayodhya.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: The temple generally remains open from 4:30 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM, with slight variations on weekends and festival days. The detailed schedule opens at 4:00 AM and closes at 9:30 PM.

faq.question: Is there any entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No. General darshan is free for all devotees. Special darshan and various sevas are available with prescribed charges (Special Darshan tickets ₹50, ₹100, and ₹250 VIP).

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: Sri Rama Navami is the most important festival, during which the famous Sri Sita Rama Kalyanam is celebrated.

faq.question: Can devotees book rooms online?
faq.answer: Yes. Temple accommodation can be booked online through the official website, subject to availability.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Bhadrachalam?
faq.answer: The ideal period is October to March, while Sri Rama Navami and Vaikunta Ekadasi are considered especially auspicious.
